title: High-Hydration Focaccia
description: A gloriously wet, no-knead focaccia with an open, airy crumb and crisp golden crust.

method.instruction: In a large bowl, mix warm water, yeast, and olive oil until the yeast fully dissolves.
Add bread flour and salt directly into the bowl. Stir with a spatula or wet hands until everything comes together. The dough will be extremely wet — this is correct.

Cover the bowl and let the dough rise until doubled in size, about 2–3 hours at room temperature. During the first hour, perform 1–2 stretch-and-folds using wet hands to help give the dough extra structure.
Generously oil a baking tin approximately 30 cm × 40 cm. Pour the dough in — no kneading required.
Using oiled fingers, gently spread the dough to the edges of the tin, creating dimples all over the surface.
Let rest for 30–45 minutes while you preheat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan-forced).
Just before baking, create more dimples with your fingertips, drizzle with olive oil, and sprinkle with sea salt flakes. Add rosemary, olives, or cherry tomatoes if desired.
Bake at 220°C for 20–25 minutes until deeply golden on top and the edges are crisp.
Cool slightly before slicing. Expect a crisp, golden crust with large, irregular holes inside.

notes.title: The Wet Dough
notes.content: This dough is so wet it is almost a batter. Do not panic — the high hydration creates those beautiful, large air pockets that make artisan-style focaccia so special. Keep your hands wet when handling it.

notes.title: Olive Oil Quality
notes.content: Use the best olive oil you can afford — focaccia absolutely shows the difference.

notes.title: Storage
notes.content: Focaccia is best on the day it is baked. Store leftovers in an airtight container for up to 2 days. Refresh in a warm oven to restore the crust.
